BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft vs. Buyer Playbook

**Rating key:** REJECT = do not accept; COUNTER = counter-propose at playbook position; ASSESS = analysis needed before a position is taken; OPEN = keep open, no concession.

**Items needing Amelia Frost's prior written approval before any movement:** the 20%/AUD 4.8M cap fallback (N-001), the 18-month claims period (N-003), and any post-completion Riverlark release (N-009). None has been given, so none may be offered.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price, AUD 4,800,000.
- **Buyer wants:** 25%, AUD 6,000,000. The 20% fallback is available only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT; COUNTER at 25%/AUD 6M.
- **Reason:** The 20% position is a conditional fallback that no one has authorised.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000 with excess-only recovery.
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT; COUNTER at playbook thresholds.
- **Reason:** The seller's thresholds are five times the buyer's and convert the basket into a deductible, which would bar most recoverable claims.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion. "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims. Fundamental/Title claims sit in a separate regime (see N-004).
- **Recommendation:** REJECT the 18-month period; COUNTER at 24 months. Reject the "applies to all Claims" wording.
- **Reason:** 18 months needs Amelia Frost's written approval, and the drafting would override the separate Title regime.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT; COUNTER with a separate Fundamental regime.
- **Reason:** Title and capacity are core to the asset. Subjecting them to general caps and a 18-month limit is inconsistent with the playbook.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature." No fraud carve-out is stated.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT; INSERT the carve-out expressly.
- **Reason:** "Any nature" language would catch fraud claims, and the playbook requires an express, non-waivable carve-out.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** Disclosure of every fact in the data room (as at 22 September 2026), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records. Schedule 7 relies on general disclosure.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT Disclosure Letter items 1.1 and 1.2 and the Schedule 7 reliance.
- **Reason:** General disclosure of the data room would undercut every specific warranty. Item 1.4 (non-admission) is acceptable only if it does not limit specific warranties.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Clause 8.3 bars claims for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the blanket exclusion. Any qualifier must name seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry. It may never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT; DELETE.
- **Reason:** The clause would let the seller avoid liability for disclosed risks that the buyer's diligence simply surfaced.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. Consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The Disclosure Letter (item 2) confirms no final consent or condition evidence has been provided. Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6M).
- **Buyer wants:** Effective consent and evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion. Not consent-on-delivery. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT; make effective consent plus condition evidence a condition precedent.
- **Reason:** Bluefen is a material customer, and the seller's version would allow Completion before the consent is effective.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** A release "to be provided following Completion." About AUD 3.2M outstanding. The facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included (item 3).
- **Buyer wants:** Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. A post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT the post-completion release; REQUIRE a payoff letter and repayment in the funds flow.
- **Reason:** A post-completion release would leave AUD 3.2M of secured debt on the company after the buyer takes ownership.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The AUD 420,000 DD-005 closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. The disclosure does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.
- **Buyer wants:** A specific funds flow line item, or seller funding. The funds flow must not silently exclude them. On-costs must be quantified.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT; REQUIRE itemisation in the funds flow, seller-funded, with on-costs quantified.
- **Reason:** Silent exclusion would leave the company liable for AUD 420,000 plus on-costs after Completion.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate." DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, which is not independently verified.
- **Buyer wants:** A broadened indemnity that preserves the SOW3 cure. Treat the AUD 180,000 as unverified until bank evidence or a confirmatory assignment is provided.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT the seller's "adequate" position; COUNTER with a broadened indemnity.
- **Reason:** SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on payment, and the seller's narrow indemnity leaves the buyer exposed on IP ownership.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material. Item 6 confirms no confirmed breach, no loss amount, and no determination of whether notification is required.
- **Buyer wants:** Preserve logs, investigate, and require regular updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** ASSESS; REQUIRE a log preservation undertaking, an investigation covenant, and regular updates.
- **Reason:** The playbook does not allow assuming a breach or loss amount, so the facts must be established through investigation.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000, described as ordinary-course operating costs. Item 8 says they should be read together for timing and scope.
- **Buyer wants:** Assessment of whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. No automatic debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** ASSESS; do not reclassify as debt or deduct from price.
- **Reason:** The disclosure does not establish the characterisation, so the buyer should assess before taking a position.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Title, capacity and Tax/IP are folded into the general regime (see N-004 and N-016).
- **Buyer wants:** Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate. No hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT.
- **Reason:** Collapsing the categories would let general caps and time limits apply to matters that require separate treatment.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the company share register at DD-012 (item 10 notes the buyer has not completed its own verification).
- **Buyer wants:** Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is a seller-supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT reliance on DD-012 alone; REQUIRE independent verification (for example, ASIC company extract and PPSR search).
- **Reason:** A seller-supplied register cannot establish title independently.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** These terms remain open. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Recommendation:** OPEN; make no concession.
- **Reason:** The seller has not justified moving Tax/IP into the general regime, and the playbook treats them as unresolved.

---

### Summary

| Ref | Issue | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| N-001 | General cap | REJECT / COUNTER 25% |
| N-002 | De minimis & basket | REJECT / COUNTER 5k / 50k |
| N-003 | Claims time limit | REJECT / COUNTER 24m |
| N-004 | Fundamental/Title | REJECT / separate regime |
| N-005 | Fraud carve-out | REJECT / insert |
| N-006 | Disclosure scope | REJECT |
| N-007 | Buyer knowledge | REJECT / delete |
| N-008 | Bluefen consent | REJECT / CP |
| N-009 | Riverlark | REJECT post-completion release |
| N-010 | Employee bonuses | REJECT / itemise |
| N-011 | Ironquay IP | REJECT / broaden |
| N-012 | Export/privacy | ASSESS / investigate |
| N-013 | Sandbar renewals | ASSESS |
| N-014 | Category separation | REJECT |
| N-015 | Title verification | REJECT reliance on DD-012 alone |
| N-016 | Tax/IP | OPEN |
